**Reasoning (as the farmer):**

I have been working this land my whole life. My husband is gone. My son comes back to help during wheat harvest and corn planting, but mostly I manage things myself or with neighbors. I have about 4 mu of flat land here in Quzhou. I know only two crops — winter wheat and summer corn. My mother grew them, I grow them, that is what this land is for.

I will not try anything new at my age. Cotton prices have been bad and it needs too much hand-picking. Vegetables would need daily attention in the market. Wheat and corn — I plant them, water them a few times, and they feed my family and bring in some cash.

For wheat, I plant in October after turning the soil with the rotary machine my neighbor brings. I buy seed from the village supply shop — the improved kind they always sell there, not the old seeds we saved before. I put down compound fertilizer at planting, then urea when the wheat is jointing in spring. I water three times: before the ground freezes, at jointing, and when the heads are filling. I spray once for weeds in winter and once for powdery mildew before heading. 

For corn, I plant right after wheat harvest in June. My son helps. We do direct seeding now, no need to plow again. I buy the hybrid seed — everyone does. Summer rains usually help so I only pump water if it is really dry around the time of tasseling. I put down a little fertilizer.

I expect maybe 430 jin per mu for wheat, 500 jin for corn. That is normal for my fields.
